_comment: Declarative list of MCP servers this machine provisions. Adding a second or third server should be a data change here, not a code change in the installer. Each server is registered with Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Pi (built-in MCP), all launching through ~/.local/bin/mcp-node.

servers.name: m365-personal-productivity
servers.description: Martin's personal Microsoft 365: Outlook calendar and mail (read + draft/create), Teams chat, SharePoint files, meeting transcripts, and mailbox organisation (categories, folders, filing)
servers._piPackageNote: Registers the checkout as a Pi package so the m365-tools skill it ships under skills/ is loaded. Claude hosts do not take packages; m365-martin tells them where to read the skill.
servers._supersedesNote: Older host keys for this same server, removed from every host on install so a machine does not end up with two registrations. 'm365' is the name this server had in Pi's mcp.json before the installer managed Pi.
servers._envNote: No secrets here. The server ships config.defaults.json with a non-secret tenant id, so a fresh clone runs without a tenant override. Set TENANT_ID here only if you need to override it - and never commit a real tenant id to this public repository; export M365_TENANT_ID before running setup instead. ALLOW_DELETE is stated explicitly even though false is already the server default: the installer writes the host env block from this file alone, so a value set by hand in a host's mcp.json is silently dropped on the next run. Record the intended posture here, not in the host. Set it to 'true' to register delete_category and delete_mail_folder and allow moving mail into Deleted Items - each still requires the server's preview-and-confirm_action approval flow. ALLOW_SEND is deliberately absent: enabling sending is a per-host decision, not a machine-wide one.
servers._dirNote: A deployment-only copy that the installer moves between tags. Never point this at the checkout you develop in: the installer refuses a checkout that is on a branch, and hosts would otherwise run whatever you last built. Develop in ~/source/... as usual; ship by tagging and bumping ref.

servers.name: memory
servers._buildNote: pnpm is pinned through npx so the build needs only node/npm, not a globally installed pnpm (Node 25+ no longer bundles corepack). Keep the version in step with packageManager in memory-mcp's package.json.
servers.description: Martin's second brain: three-tier markdown memory (core, archive, bank) over the local DailyDriver data repo, with a one-way publish path
servers._hostsNote: Pi only, matching how it was registered by hand before. Claude Desktop is planned as a later read surface; widen this list deliberately, since writes are enabled.
servers._requiresNote: The data repo is never provisioned from here (this repository is public). The installer warns if it is missing; the server refuses to start without it.
servers._envNote: MEMORY_ALLOW_WRITE=true keeps the posture it had when registered by hand; writes are still staged inside the server. env values are expanded with $HOME by the installer because GUI hosts do not expand variables.
